text:
Ethan (Customer): Hi team — vendor security questionnaire landed from procurement. They want confirmation on whether Redwood retains raw customer inputs in logs and for how long, KMS/HSM details, and if Dedicated keeps data entirely in-customer. Questionnaire ID VQ-992.

Sofia (CS): Thanks @Ethan — looping in @Arjun and @Nora. We'll triage and send a consolidated response + evidence. Any hard blockers?

Arjun (Security): Short answer now: Hosted API does not persist raw request payloads beyond short-term operational logs (default 7 days). Customers can opt out of logging or set retention to 0 where configured. Dedicated and Private: requests and KV caches live in customer-controlled infrastructure; Redwood does not retain plaintext customer data or manage customer keys unless customer configures Redwood-managed KMS. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and provide HSM integration options for Private deployments.

Nora (Legal): For the DPA language: Redwood acts as a Processor. We'll provide the standard DPA clause and subprocessors list. Note: SOC2 Type II report is shared as an attestation letter under NDA / secure portal; we can't publish raw SOC2 report. We'll also prepare a bridge letter if timelines require.

Sofia (CS): Can you paste the exact retention & KMS wording I can copy into the questionnaire? Customer will likely copy-paste.

Arjun (Security): Paste snippet you can use: 
```
Retention: Redwood Inference retains request logs for up to 7 days by default for operational debugging and abuse detection. Customers may opt out of logging or configure retention via account settings. Dedicated and Private deployments keep request data within the customer's network boundary and do not persist request payloads to Redwood-managed long-term storage.
Encryption: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. Key management supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and customer-provided keys for Private deployments. HSM-backed key storage is available for on-prem packages where required.
```

Nora (Legal): Add this DPA-friendly line as well: 
```
Data Processing: Redwood acts as a Processor under the DPA. A current list of subprocessors and our Data Processing Addendum are available at https://redwood.ai/subprocessors and will be provided to the customer under the DPA. SOC2 Type II attestation is available via secure portal/NDA; we can provide a redacted attestation letter for procurement review.
```

Sofia (CS): Perfect, thanks. I'll assemble the response and upload supporting docs. Planning to attach: redwood_service_description.pdf and soc2_attestation_letter.pdf (via secure portal link).

Ethan (Customer): Quick follow-up: for Dedicated, do you still collect any telemetry back to Redwood (billing/health)? Need to confirm for our security team.

Arjun (Security): Minimal aggregated telemetry only: instance health metrics (uptime, CPU/GPU usage), billing meters. These metrics are not tied to request payloads and are used for capacity/billing/operational health. We can provide a signed statement for the customer's security team.

Sofia (CS): I'll set up a 30-min call to review with the customer tomorrow at 11:00am PT. @Nora can you confirm SOC2 letter share via portal before the call? @Arjun can you prepare the telemetry statement?

Nora (Legal): Confirmed — SOC2 attestation letter will be uploaded to the secure portal by EOD today.

Arjun (Security): Will draft a 1-paragraph signed telemetry statement and upload to the portal before the call.

redwood-docs-bot: Uploaded files: redwood_service_description.pdf, soc2_attestation_letter.pdf to secure portal (link shared in DM).

Sofia (CS): Status: drafting final questionnaire answers, evidence uploaded to portal, scheduling call. ETA to send consolidated response to procurement: today by 18:00 PT. :thumbsup:

Ethan (Customer): Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.
